q: Maximum bending moment occurs at the centre if the simply supported beam is subjected to
options: uniformly distributed load throughout the span
triangular load with maximum intensity at centre
explanation: All three symmetric loading patterns produce maximum BM at mid-span for a simply supported beam.

q: Find the maximum SF induced in a S.S beam if the beam is subjected to a point load of 4 KN at the centre of beam and span of the beam is 4 m
explanation: Each support reaction = W/2 = 4/2 = 2 kN, which is the maximum shear force.

q: Which one is correct if the deflection of a beam is y
explanation: All are standard beam-deflection relations: slope θ=dy/dx, curvature dθ/dx=d²y/dx², and M=EI/R.

q: If y is the deflection of the beam, then shear force is
explanation: V = EI·d³y/dx³ — shear force is the third derivative of deflection (times EI).

q: The relation between deflection (y) and bending moment (M) is
explanation: The Euler-Bernoulli beam equation: M = -EI·d²y/dx² (sign convention dependent).

q: The relation between the radius of curvature (R), bending moment (M) and flexural rigidity (EI) is given by
explanation: From the bending equation: M/I = E/R, so M = EI/R.

q: In simple bending theory, the assumption that plane section before bending remains plane after bending implies that
options: stress is proportional to strain at all sections
strain is proportional to the distance from the natural axis
stress is uniform in the cross-section
explanation: The plane-sections assumption directly implies a linear strain distribution across the depth, proportional to distance from the neutral axis.

q: Along the neutral axis of a simply supported beam
options: the fibres are subjected to maximum stress
explanation: By definition, the neutral axis is the locus of zero bending stress/strain.

q: Simple bending equation is
explanation: The standard bending equation: M/I = f/y = E/R.

q: Maximum bending moment occurs where
options: shear force is less than one
explanation: Since V=dM/dx, M is at an extremum (max/min) where V=0, i.e. where the shear force diagram crosses zero and changes sign.

q: In a beam where shear force is maximum the bending moment will be
explanation: As per the answer key; there's no fixed universal relation between the location of max SF and the BM value there — it depends on the specific loading case.

q: Shape of bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam having point load at centre is
explanation: BM varies linearly from zero at supports to maximum under the point load — forming a triangle.

q: Bending moment diagram of simply supported beam having uniformly distributed load is
explanation: BM under UDL varies as a second-degree curve (parabola), zero at supports, maximum at mid-span.

q: The variation of the bending moment in the portion of the beam carrying linearly varying load is
explanation: A linearly varying load (triangular) produces a shear force that's parabolic and a bending moment that's cubic in x.

q: The variation of the bending moment in the segment of a beam where the load is uniformly distributed is
explanation: Under UDL, shear varies linearly and bending moment (its integral) varies parabolically.

q: The bending moment diagram for a cantilever beam subjected to a moment at the end of the beam would be
explanation: A pure end moment with no other loads produces a constant BM throughout — a rectangle.

q: A beam simply supported at ends is subjected to load. The maximum bending moment is located where
explanation: Since dM/dx = V, BM is maximum/minimum exactly where V = 0.

q: Point of contraflexure is a point where bending moment
explanation: At a point of contraflexure the bending moment passes through zero, changing from sagging to hogging (or vice versa).

q: In a continuous beam, the point where bending moment changes sign is called
explanation: All three terms describe the same location where BM sign reverses.

q: The point of contraflexure occurs in a beam
explanation: Contraflexure points typically arise in overhanging beams (and continuous beams), where sagging and hogging regions meet.

q: In a fixed beam, the points of contraflexure,
options: for a moment applied load are 2
explanation: Fixed beams develop two points of contraflexure for each of these standard load cases.

q: In case of a fixed beam loaded at its centre, the number of points at which BM is zero
explanation: A centrally-loaded fixed beam has two points of contraflexure (zero BM), symmetric about mid-span.

q: The maximum bending moment caused by a moving load on a simply supported beam is
explanation: For a single moving point load, the maximum BM occurs directly under the load at its critical position.

q: The maximum bending moment caused by a moving load on a fixed end beam occurs
explanation: For a fixed-end beam, the largest bending moment from a moving load typically develops at the supports (fixed ends).

q: If a cantilever beam carries a uniformly distributed load over its entire length, then the shape of the shear force diagram and bending moment diagram respectively are
explanation: Under UDL, SF is linear (triangle) and BM is a second-degree (quadratic) parabola.

q: The variation of the bending moment in the segment of a beam where no external load is present is
explanation: With zero load, shear force is constant, so BM (its integral) varies linearly.

q: The critical bending moment caused in a fixed end beam loaded with a uniformly distributed load (W=wL) throughout is
explanation: For a fixed-fixed beam under UDL, the fixed-end (support) moment = WL/12.

q: The maximum bending moment caused by a large number of equally spaced identical loads on a simply supported beam is (W=wL)
explanation: As the number of equal point loads increases, the loading approaches a UDL, so max BM approaches WL/8.

q: The maximum bending moment caused by a moment M applied at a distance 'a' from one end on a simply supported beam is (where L=span, a>L/2)
explanation: As per the answer key for this specific case (a > L/2).

q: For a beam of uniform strength if its depth is maintained constant then its width will vary in proportion to
explanation: As per the answer key for this set (uniform-strength beam with constant depth).

q: In a simply supported beam with span (L) having a triangular load with its intensity 0 at both ends and W at center. The maximum BM will be
explanation: As per the answer key for this symmetric triangular loading case.

q: Maximum deflection of a simply supported beam subjected to concentrated load (w) at the mid point is
explanation: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/48EI for a central point load on a simply supported beam.

q: In a simply supported beam with span L subjected to a point load W at center, find the maximum bending moment induced in the beam
explanation: M_max = WL/4 for a central point load on a simply supported beam.

q: A simply supported beam of length l carries a load varying uniformly from zero at left end to maximum at right end. Maximum bending moment occurs at a distance of
explanation: For a triangular (0 to max) UDL, the max BM occurs at x = L/√3 measured from the zero-load end.

q: Load carrying capacity of fixed beam is
options: greater than simply supported beam and cantilever beam
explanation: Fixed-end restraint reduces the maximum bending moment for a given load, allowing a fixed beam to carry more load than an equivalent simply supported or cantilever beam.

q: Determinate beam can be analyzed with the help of
explanation: A statically determinate beam can be fully solved using the three equations of static equilibrium (ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0, ΣM=0).

q: A beam fixed at both ends with a central load W in the middle will have zero bending moment at
explanation: A fixed-fixed beam with central point load develops two points of contraflexure (zero BM), symmetric about mid-span.

q: The maximum bending moment caused on a simply supported beam subjected to two equal concentrated loads (W/2) spaced at equal distance (L/3) over the span is
explanation: For this standard two-point-load arrangement at the third-points, max BM = WL/6.

q: A beam is said to be of uniform strength if
options: bending moment is same throughout the beam
deflection is same throughout the beam
bending stress is same throughout the beam
explanation: As per the answer key for this set (note: the classic textbook definition of 'uniform strength' is usually stated as constant bending stress throughout — worth double-checking against your source book if this seems inconsistent).

q: A section of a beam is said to be in pure bending if it is subjected to
options: constant bending moment and constant shear force
constant bending moment and zero shear force
constant shear force and zero bending moment
explanation: As per the answer key for this set (note: the standard textbook definition of pure bending is constant BM with zero shear force — worth double-checking against your source book, as this may be a possible key erratum).

q: The maximum deflection of a beam occurs at
explanation: Maximum deflection occurs where the slope of the elastic curve (dy/dx) is zero.

q: The slope of an elastic curve at the point of contraflexure
explanation: At a contraflexure point, only BM=0 is guaranteed; the slope can take any value there.

q: If the length of a simply supported beam carrying a concentrated load at the centre is doubled, the deflection at the center will become
explanation: Since δ ∝ L³, doubling the span increases deflection by a factor of 2³ = 8.

q: The maximum deflection in a cantilever beam carrying a concentrated load 'w' at the free end
explanation: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/3EI for a cantilever with a point load at the free end.

q: The maximum deflection in a cantilever beam carrying uniformly distributed load (w) over its span
explanation: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/8EI for a cantilever under UDL (W = total load = wL).

q: The maximum deflection of a simply supported beam subjected to concentrated load (W) at the mid point is
explanation: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/48EI for a central point load.

q: The maximum deflection of a simply supported beam subjected to uniformly distributed load (w) over the span is
explanation: Standard formula: δ_max = 5WL³/384EI for UDL on a simply supported beam (W = total load = wL).

q: The diagram showing the variation of BM along the span of a beam is called
explanation: By definition, a Bending Moment Diagram (BMD) plots BM variation along the span. (Double-check this against your printed key — some editions mismark this answer.)
